sentences.text: This criminal revision under Section 438 r/w 442 of the BNSS, 2023 is preferred being aggrieved by the order dated 18/10/2024 passed in RCT No.637/2021 by the JMFC, Rajgarh whereby the charges under Section 498A of the IPC has been framed against the revision petitioner No.1 Narhari and charges under Section 498A of the IPC has been framed against the revision petitioner No.2 Radha in a case arising out of Crime No.326/2021 registered at Police Station Rajgarh, District Rajgarh.
02. Facts of the case in brief are that the complainant was married to the son of the revision petitioners in the year 1995.
A written complaint dated 16.06.2021 was referred to the In-charge Police Station Kotwali Rajgarh alleging the cruelty and keeping her Streedhan.
The offence under Section 498A, 406 r/w 34 of the IPC was registered against the revision petitioners and their son Girish Parpan.

The report was submitted under NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37460 2 CRR-154-2025 Section 498A, 406 r/w 34 and 323 of the IPC.
03.

Vide order dated 18.10.2024, the charges under Section 498A and 323 of the IPC were framed against the husband of the complainant, who is the son of the present revision petitioner and the charges mentioned in para 1 were framed against the revision petitioners.

04. Challenging the order of framing of charge against the revision petitioners, this revision petition has been preferred on the ground that the complainant and her husband lived together for almost 25 years.
There is no specific time and place of the so called acts and cruelty or keeping the Streedhan.
The complainant is a Government teacher in Unhel, District Ujjain and resides in Unhel, District Ujjain but has lodged the report in Rajgarh.

This report is a counterblast of the reports lodged by Girish Parpan against his son for committing robbery, and this complaint was made in order to put Narhari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196963411/
1 pressure on the revision petitioners.

sentences.text: The revision petitioner No.1 Narhari is a retired Deputy Collector and is aged about 87 years, and revision petitioner No.2 is aged about 81 years and are having problem in walking.

The application of Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed by the son of the revision petitioners against the complainant in the Nagda Court, District Ujjain, in that case the matter was settled, but the report has been referred.
Heard.
05. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the revision petition.

06. Perused the final report and the material collected during the investigation and filed with the final report.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37460 3 CRR-154-2025 07.
The list of documents contains 11 documents in number, and total 4 statements of the witnesses.
The witnesses are the complainant Garima & her 21 year old son Suyash, Piyush Vaishnav and Manoj.
The document at Serial No.3 is the list of Streedhan prepared on 16.06.2021.
There are 3 photographs and 3 letters written by the petitioner No.1 alongwith 5 typed pages.

In the first 3 paras, there is no mention regarding any act of cruelty by the petitioners. There is a mention of dispute between husband and wife. In the last 4 paragraphs, there is a mention of the revision petitioners but there is no specific dates regarding the acts attributed to the petitioners.
There is no specific allegation regarding the acts attributed to the revision petitioners in the statement of 21 year old son, who is a student of law in Government New Law College, Indore.
The letters written by the petitioner No.1 does not refer the act of cruelty.
10. Having considered the above-discussed matter in total, this court is of the opinion that none of the ingredients of Section 498A, 406 of the IPC is made out against the revision petitioners.

Accordingly, the revision petition is allowed and the order dated 18.12.2024 passed in RCT No.637/2021 by Judical Magistrate First Class, Rajgarh whereby the charges under Section 498A of the IPC has been framed against the revision petitioner No.1 Narhari NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:37460 5 CRR-154-2025 and charges under Section 498A & 406 of the IPC has been framed against the revision petitioner No.2 Radha are hereby set aside and the revision petitioners are discharged from the aforesaid charges.
11.
In view of the aforesaid, the revision petition stands allowed and disposed off.
12. A copy of this order be sent to the learned trial Court for information.
Certified copy, as per rules.
